MUJAHID:v2p679/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p679/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p679/r1.claim: Mujahid says the Day of mutual loss is when the people of Paradise cause the people of Hell to lose.

MUQATIL:64:9-10/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:64:9-10/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:64:9-10/r1.claim: The Day of Gathering brings together the people of heaven and earth; it is the day believers in guidance deprive the people of error, as one group enters Paradise and another the Fire.

MUQATIL:64:9-10/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:64:9-10/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:64:9-10/r2.claim: Belief in God's oneness and righteous action efface sins and bring eternal gardens with rivers; this is the great success.

MAJAZ:v2p260/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p260/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p260/r1.claim: Man has singular form but collective meaning, so the following khālidīn is plural.

TAB-FULL:v23p10/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p10/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p10/r1.claim: God gathers all creatures for judgment; that day is mutual loss, as the people of Paradise gain against the people of Hell.

TAB-FULL:v23p10/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p10/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p10/r2.claim: Mujāhid explains the Day of Mutual Loss as the people of Paradise gaining over the people of Hell.

TAB-FULL:v23p10/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p10/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p10/r3.claim: Qatāda says the gathering and mutual-loss day is the Day of Resurrection, when Paradise's people gain over Hell's.

TAB-FULL:v23p10/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p10/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p10/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās calls it one of the names of Resurrection, magnified by God as a warning to His servants.

TAB-FULL:v23p11/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p11/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p11/r1.claim: Whoever believes in God, obeys His commands, and avoids His prohibitions has sins erased and enters gardens with rivers below, remaining there forever; this is the great triumph.

ZAJJAJ:v5p180/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p180/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p180/r2.claim: Yawma is an adverb linked to the promise that people will be resurrected and told what they did: on the day of gathering.

ZAJJAJ:v5p180/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p180/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p180/r3.claim: The Day of Mutual Loss is when the people of Paradise gain over the people of the Fire and higher-ranked residents of Paradise gain over those below them.

ZAJJAJ:v5p180/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p180/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p180/r4.claim: This loss is illustrated as a commercial bargain: faith and the purchase of guidance bring salvation, unlike those who bought misguidance.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3358#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3358#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3358#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Day of Mutual Loss is one of the names of Resurrection Day.

NAHHAS:v4p443/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p443/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p443/r4.claim: Yawm is governed by tunabbaʾūn; the pronoun in yajmaʿukum refers to God, not the Day, since a day cannot be annexed to a verb whose pronoun points back to it.

NAHHAS:v4p443/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p443/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p443/r5.claim: Dhālika yawmu al-tagābun is a subject-predicate clause; outside the Qur'anic reading, yawma may be an accusative temporal adverb.

NAHHAS:v4p443/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p443/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p443/r6.claim: The clause 'whoever believes and does good' is coordinated; yaʿmal may instead be raised as a circumstantial clause.

NAHHAS:v4p443/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p443/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p443/r7.claim: God erases sins and admits believers to gardens; khālidīna is circumstantial, abadan temporal, and al-fawz means salvation.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p295/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p295/r1.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p295/r1.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read both verbs with first-person plural nūn, speaking of God's forgiveness and admission into the gardens.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p295/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p295/r2.speaker: الباقون
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p295/r2.claim: The other readers use third-person يَدْخُلْهُ, returning to the explicit preceding subject; the nūn shift is supported by a similar shift in the account of Moses.

SULAMI:v2p330#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p330#3/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p330#3/r1.claim: People of obedience outstrip people of disobedience; among people of truth, degrees of loss reflect degrees of light at vision and manifestation, with heart's sight exceeding the eye's.

SULAMI:v2p330#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p330#3/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p330#3/r2.claim: Heart's vision is greater than sight because the eye is limited in contemplation; when the Real appears, each person is silenced from speech and disputation.

THALABI:v9p328#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p328#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p328#2/r1.claim: Medinan and Syrian readers use first-person plural verbs for forgiving sins and admitting to Paradise; the other readers use third-person singular verbs.

THALABI:v9p328#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p328#2/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p328#2/r2.claim: A calamity occurs by God's will and decree; faith guides the heart to certainty that what struck could not have missed and what missed could not have struck, as Ibn Abbas says.

THALABI:v9p328#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p328#2/r3.speaker: علقمة
THALABI:v9p328#2/r3.claim: Alqama says the guided believer suffers a calamity, recognizes it as from God, and accepts it with contentment and submission.

THALABI:v9p328#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p328#2/r4.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
THALABI:v9p328#2/r4.claim: Abu Bakr al-Warraq says faith during ease guides to gratitude, while faith during hardship guides to acceptance and patience.

THALABI:v9p328#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p328#2/r5.speaker: أبو عثمان الجيري
THALABI:v9p328#2/r5.claim: Abu Uthman al-Jiri says sound faith guides the heart to following the Prophetic practice.

THALABI:v9p328#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p328#2/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p328#2/r6.claim: The common reading has ya and fatḥa in 'yahdi qalbahu'; al-Sulami reads it passive with ḍamma, Talha reads first-person plural, and Ikrima reads 'yahda' as becoming still.

THALABI:v9p328#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p328#2/r7.speaker: مالك بن دينار
THALABI:v9p328#2/r7.claim: Malik ibn Dinar reads 'yahda qalbuhu' with a long alif replacing the hamza.

THALABI:v9p328/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p328/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p328/r1.claim: The Day of Mutual Loss is named with the verbal form of loss: the day when people forfeit their share or advantage.

THALABI:v9p328/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p328/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v9p328/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that every believer shown the place in Hell he would have had by wrongdoing grows more grateful, while each person in Hell shown his possible place in Paradise grows more regretful.

THALABI:v9p328/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p328/r3.speaker: المفسرون
THALABI:v9p328/r3.claim: The commentators say unbelievers lose their homes and families in Paradise through unbelief, while believers regret their shortcomings and wasted days.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p22/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p22/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p22/r10.claim: Another possibility links taghābun to concealment: God hid the day, and the term also applies to hidden body folds and concealed fraud.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p22/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p22/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p22/r2.claim: The gathering is the Day of Resurrection.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p22/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p22/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p22/r3.claim: It is called the Day of Gathering because each prophet and community are gathered together.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p22/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p22/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p22/r4.claim: Alternatively, wrongdoers and wronged people are gathered together.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p22/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p22/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p22/r5.claim: A further possibility is that reward for obedience and punishment for sins are brought together.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p22/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p22/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p22/r6.claim: Yawm al-Taghābun is one name for Resurrection; a poem uses it in this sense.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p22/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p22/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p22/r7.claim: It may be named for Paradise's people outgaining those in the Fire.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p22/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p22/r8.speaker: الشاعر
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p22/r8.claim: A poem depicts true loss as deception of the intellect.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p22/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p22/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p22/r9.claim: The wronged may outgain wrongdoers after worldly deprivation.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p485#4/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p485#4/r1.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p485#4/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses يوم as accusative governed by the promise that people will be raised and informed.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p485#4/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p485#4/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p485#4/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil say the gathering is the Resurrection, when the inhabitants of heaven and earth are assembled.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p485#4/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p485#4/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p485#4/r3.claim: Taghabun is mutual loss or being cheated in buying and selling, when someone takes an item for less than its value.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p485#4/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p485#4/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p485#4/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas begins to explain the mutual loss as some people suffering in Hell while others enjoy Paradise.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:64:9/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:64:9/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:64:9/r1.claim: The Day of Mutual Loss shows the loss of disbelievers who forfeit the Paradise places they would have had if they believed, and of believers whose lesser rank reveals their shortcomings.

JISHUMI:v10p6954/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6954/r1.speaker: يعقوب
JISHUMI:v10p6954/r1.claim: Yaqub reads najmaʿukum with first-person plural, aligning it with the first-person verb anzalnā.

JISHUMI:v10p6954/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6954/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p6954/r2.claim: The remaining readers use the third-person verb yajmaʿukum, referring to God's name.

JISHUMI:v10p6954/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6954/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وابن عامر
JISHUMI:v10p6954/r3.claim: They read nukaffir and nudkhil with first-person plural; the remaining readers use third-person forms.

JISHUMI:v10p6954/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6954/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p6954/r4.claim: Ghubn is loss or shortchanging; taghābun is mutual loss, originally used of buying and selling when something is taken below its value.

JISHUMI:v10p6954/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6954/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p6954/r5.claim: One who trades the afterlife for the world is cheated by taking something trivial in exchange for something precious; the people of Hell are cheated by Paradise's people.

JISHUMI:v10p6954/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6954/r6.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v10p6954/r6.claim: An alternative etymology connects ghubn with concealing something, as in the hidden recesses called maghābin.

JISHUMI:v10p6954/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6954/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p6954/r7.claim: Yawm may be accusative as a time expression, or as an exhortation to remember the day and prepare for it.

JISHUMI:v10p6955/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6955/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p6955/r10.claim: A further view is that people in Paradise outdo one another in the increase of their ranks.

JISHUMI:v10p6955/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6955/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p6955/r11.claim: God erases the sins of believers who do good, admits them to gardens with rivers, and grants them eternal residence; this is great success, attaining what is sought and escaping harm.

JISHUMI:v10p6955/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6955/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p6955/r6.claim: God may gather people from their graves toward Judgment, or gather them on Judgment Day because all creatures assemble there.

JISHUMI:v10p6955/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6955/r7.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد
JISHUMI:v10p6955/r7.claim: One interpretation says the people of Paradise cheat the people of Hell by winning the good outcome.

JISHUMI:v10p6955/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6955/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p6955/r8.claim: Another interpretation says the people of Hell lose by choosing transient worldly life and thereby forfeiting the far more valuable reward.

JISHUMI:v10p6955/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6955/r9.speaker: أبو هريرة
JISHUMI:v10p6955/r9.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits a Prophetic report that each believer entering Paradise is shown the Hell seat they would have occupied by wrongdoing, while each person entering Hell is shown the Paradise seat they would have had by doing good, increasing gratitude or regret.

JISHUMI:v10p6956/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6956/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p6956/r3.claim: All creation is gathered at Judgment, hence the name Day of Gathering; it is called Mutual Loss because the people of Hell forfeit Paradise's reward and enter the Fire.

JISHUMI:v10p6956/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6956/r4.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v10p6956/r4.claim: The verse indicates that human acts originate with people; if God created them, mutual loss would not make sense, just as it would not for bodily forms.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p141#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p141#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p141#2/r6.claim: The Gathering is Resurrection, when heaven and earth’s inhabitants are assembled; mutual loss is missing one’s share, especially Paradise’s family and homes.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p141#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p141#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p141#2/r7.claim: Every unbeliever loses by abandoning faith, while each believer loses in proportion to shortcomings in good works.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p141#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p141#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p141#2/r8.claim: Readers in Medina and Syria use first-person plural ‘We forgive’ and ‘We admit’; the other readers use third-person forms.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p319#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p319#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p319#2/r2.claim: Yawm yajmaʿukum may attach grammatically to the earlier promise that people will be informed or to khabīr; God knows on every day but singles out the day when that knowledge harms them.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p319#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p319#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p319#3/r1.claim: Most read yajmaʿukum with a vowel on ʿayn; Abū ʿAmr allows it to be silent, while Salām and Yaʿqūb read najmaʿukum with God's first-person plural.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p319#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p319#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p319#3/r2.claim: The Gathering is Resurrection: each rises hoping for rank, then believers gain Paradise and disbelievers the Fire, so believers are the winners; taghābun is not grammatically reciprocal, like tawāḍuʿ and taḥāmul.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p319#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p319#3/r3.speaker: نافع وابن عامر والمفضل عن عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p319#3/r3.claim: These authorities read nukaffir and nudkhil with nūn of majesty; other reciters use yāʾ, meaning God absolves and admits.

TABRISI:64:9-10/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:64:9-10/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:64:9-10/r1.claim: Faith and righteous deeds cause God to erase sins and admit people to eternally flowing gardens; this is unsurpassed success.

TABRISI:64:9/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:64:9/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:64:9/r1.claim: The Day of Gathering is Judgment Day, when earlier and later peoples are assembled for resurrection and requital.

TABRISI:64:9/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:64:9/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:64:9/r2.claim: Ghubn is an exchange in which someone takes the worse and leaves the better, or takes the better and leaves the worse: believers give up worldly share for the afterlife, while unbelievers choose the reverse and are cheated.

TABRISI:64:9/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:64:9/r3.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد
TABRISI:64:9/r3.claim: Alternatively, the Day of Mutual Loss is when the people of Paradise outgain the people of Hell.

TABRISI:64:9/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:64:9/r4.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:64:9/r4.claim: The Prophet said each believer is shown the place in Hell they would have occupied had they done wrong, increasing gratitude; each person in Hell sees their lost place in Paradise, increasing regret.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p282#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p282#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p282#3/r1.claim: The phrase yauma yajmaʿukum is governed by the earlier statement that people will surely be resurrected and told what they did; the Gathering is Judgment Day.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p282#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p282#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p282#3/r2.claim: It is called the Day of Gathering because God brings together jinn, humans, the inhabitants of heaven, and the people of earth.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p282#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p282#3/r3.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p282#3/r3.claim: Taghābun means the unbeliever is cheated of his share when a believer inherits his home and family in Paradise.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p282#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p282#3/r4.speaker: مجاهد والقرظي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p282#3/r4.claim: Taghābun means the people of Paradise have gained at the expense of the people of Hell.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p282#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p282#3/r5.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p282#3/r5.claim: Taghābun is the wrongdoer's loss to the wronged person: the wronged person, cheated in worldly life, becomes the winner in the afterlife.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p282#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p282#3/r6.speaker: الثعلبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p282#3/r6.claim: The Day reveals the unbeliever's loss for abandoning faith and the believer's loss through falling short in good works.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p282#3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p282#3/r7.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p282#3/r7.claim: The term is a commercial metaphor, like the descriptions of a failed or successful trade.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p282#3/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p282#3/r8.speaker: نافع وابن عامر والمفضل عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p282#3/r8.claim: They recite the verbs for covering sins and admitting believers with nūn in both forms.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p282#3/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p282#3/r9.speaker: الباقون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p282#3/r9.claim: The other readers recite both verbs with yāʾ.

QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#2/r1.claim: The people of Paradise trade worldly life for the afterlife, while the people of the Fire trade the afterlife for worldly life; this is figurative exchange and loss.

QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#2/r2.claim: God divided people between Paradise and Fire and assigned everyone a dwelling in both; the guided may inherit the place of the forsaken, producing the ultimate exchange.

QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#2/r3.claim: This exchange may also be described as inheritance, as explained under the opening of al-Mu’minun.

QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#2/r4.claim: Loss can occur before Judgment, but this verse concerns the final loss whose consequences cannot be repaired.

QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#2/r5.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#2/r5.claim: They report three losses: discarded knowledge later practiced by a student, ill-gotten wealth wisely used by an heir, and an obedient slave saved while his sinful master is ruined.

QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#2/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#2/r6.claim: A report describes a husband condemned for unlawful earnings and neglecting support, while his wife is admitted to Paradise and tells him their fates have been exchanged.

QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#3/r1.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#3/r1.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says the verse’s restriction of mutual loss to Judgment Day proves worldly transaction loss is impermissible; the Baghdadis would rescind a sale when the loss exceeds one-third.

QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#3/r2.speaker: البغداديون
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#3/r2.claim: The Baghdadi jurists support rescission for substantial loss with the Prophet’s instruction to Hibbān ibn Munqidh to disclaim fraud and retain a three-day option.

QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#3/r3.claim: Qurtubi says fraud is religiously forbidden by consensus, but slight loss cannot be avoided; substantial avoidable loss warrants rescission, with one-third set by analogy to bequests.

QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#3/r4.claim: One interpretation takes the verse to mean that unrestricted loss is permitted only on that Day.

QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#3/r5.claim: Alternatively, it means irreparable loss: worldly losses may be reversed or offset by later profit, whereas losing Paradise can never be recovered.

QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#3/r6.speaker: بعض علماء الصوفية
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#3/r6.claim: Some Sufi scholars say everyone meets God at a loss because no one can fully perform enough works to receive complete recompense.

QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#3/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#3/r7.claim: A report says everyone meets God regretful: the wrongdoer regrets failing to do good, and the good-doer regrets failing to do more.

QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#4/r1.claim: Nafi and Ibn Amir read both verbs in the first-person plural; the other readers use the third-person form.

QURTUBI-FULL:64:9/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9/r1.claim: The time expression may be governed by “you will be informed,” by “all-knowing” with its warning sense, or by an implied command to remember.

QURTUBI-FULL:64:9/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9/r10.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9/r10.claim: Al-Zajjāj says even a believer is at a loss when someone else is elevated to a higher rank in Paradise.

QURTUBI-FULL:64:9/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9/r11.claim: The question about what transaction caused this loss introduces an answer that it is a parable of buying and selling.

QURTUBI-FULL:64:9/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9/r2.claim: Ghubn means a shortfall in a transaction, taking something from someone for less than its value.

QURTUBI-FULL:64:9/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9/r3.speaker: قراءة العامة
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9/r3.claim: The common reading says yajmaʿukum with yāʾ, matching the preceding mention of God's name and the report that God knows what people do.

QURTUBI-FULL:64:9/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9/r4.speaker: نصر وابن أبي إسحاق والجحدري ويعقوب وسلام
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9/r4.claim: They read najmaʿukum with nūn, echoing the first-person plural in “the light We sent down.”

QURTUBI-FULL:64:9/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9/r5.claim: The Day of Gathering brings together the first and last generations, humans and jinn, and inhabitants of heaven and earth.

QURTUBI-FULL:64:9/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9/r6.claim: Other interpretations say it gathers each servant with their deeds, wrongdoer with victim, each prophet with their community, or reward with punishment.

QURTUBI-FULL:64:9/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9/r7.claim: The Day of Mutual Loss is Resurrection Day: Paradise's people gain the Garden while Hell's people receive the Fire after exchanging good for evil, quality for poor, and bliss for torment.

QURTUBI-FULL:64:9/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9/r8.claim: The commercial idiom means the loser takes less in a sale or purchase while the other side prevails; related words describe excess cloth cut away and folds of the body.

QURTUBI-FULL:64:9/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9/r9.speaker: المفسرون
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9/r9.claim: The truly shortchanged person is deprived of their family and homes in Paradise; every disbeliever loses by abandoning faith, and every believer loses through deficient goodness and wasted days.

BAYDAWI-FULL:64:7-9/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:64:7-9/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:64:7-9/r5.claim: يوم يجمعكم may be attached to the promise of being informed or mean an implied remember; Yaʿqūb reads نجمعكم.

BAYDAWI-FULL:64:7-9/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:64:7-9/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:64:7-9/r6.claim: The gathering is for reckoning and recompense and includes angels, humans, and jinn; it is the Day of mutual loss, when people discover the lasting stakes of one another’s possible stations.

BAYDAWI-FULL:64:7-9/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:64:7-9/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:64:7-9/r7.claim: The image of traders mutually losing highlights that true loss concerns the lasting afterlife; believers’ sins are erased and they enter eternal gardens, the combined removal of harm and receipt of benefit.

BAYDAWI-FULL:64:7-9/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:64:7-9/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:64:7-9/r8.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read both verbs with نون.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p252#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p252#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p252#2/r1.claim: “The day” is governed by “you will be informed,” or invites the listener to remember the day everyone is gathered.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p252#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p252#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p252#2/r2.claim: Mutual loss is like losing a trade: the blessed occupy places the damned would have had, and the damned lose places they might have had; this is true loss, unlike worldly loss.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p252#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p252#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p252#2/r3.claim: “Whoever believes and does good” describes a source of action; the Medinan and Syrian readings use first-person plural for “We erase” and “We admit.”

QASHANI:64:9-11/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:64:9-11/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:64:9-11/r1.claim: Worldly possessions are inevitably transient, so their loss is no real fraud; true loss is wasting enduring capital, the light of readiness and perfection, and regret appears on Judgment Day.

QASHANI:64:9-11/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:64:9-11/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:64:9-11/r2.claim: Wasting innate readiness and its light is absolute loss; keeping readiness but failing to reach its full potential is relative loss beside the perfected person, like a lost trade.

QASHANI:64:9-11/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:64:9-11/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:64:9-11/r3.claim: Imitative faith, avoiding sins, and ordinary obedience expiate sins and lead to gardens of the self according to one’s deeds.

QASHANI:64:9-11/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:64:9-11/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:64:9-11/r4.claim: Verified faith, renouncing one’s qualities, and following God’s qualities expiate psychic traits and lead to gardens of the heart; witnessed faith and vigilance about existence lead to the spirit’s gardens.

QASHANI:64:9-11/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:64:9-11/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:64:9-11/r5.claim: True faith and vigilance about selfhood and witnessing its annihilation expiate residual ego and its shifts, leading to gardens of the divine Essence.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p186/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p186/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p186/r1.claim: Taghābun derives from loss-making but is not reciprocal between two parties here; it is one-sided, like tawāḍaʿa and taḥāmala.

SAMIN-DURR:64:9/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:64:9/r1.speaker: النحاس
SAMIN-DURR:64:9/r1.claim: Al-Nahhas attaches يوم يجمعكم to لتنبؤن.

SAMIN-DURR:64:9/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:64:9/r2.speaker: الحوفي
SAMIN-DURR:64:9/r2.claim: Al-Hawfi attaches يوم يجمعكم to خبير.

SAMIN-DURR:64:9/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:64:9/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:64:9/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari supplies an implicit اذكر, making يوم يجمعكم a direct object.

SAMIN-DURR:64:9/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:64:9/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:64:9/r4.claim: Abu al-Baqa attaches the phrase to an implied clause: you will differ in standing on the day He gathers you.

SAMIN-DURR:64:9/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:64:9/r5.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:64:9/r5.claim: The common reading has fatḥa on yāʾ and ḍamma on ʿayn; Abu Amr is also reported with sukūn and an assimilated or colored ʿayn, as in 67:20.

SAMIN-DURR:64:9/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:64:9/r6.speaker: يعقوب وسلام وزيد بن علي والشعبي
SAMIN-DURR:64:9/r6.claim: These readers use the first-person plural نجمعكم, We gather you.

SAMIN-DURR:64:9/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:64:9/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:64:9/r7.claim: التغابن is a reciprocal form from commercial loss, metaphorically taking something below its value; alternatively الغبن means concealment, as in a hidden sale, and the form can describe a one-sided action.

SAMIN-DURR:64:9/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:64:9/r8.speaker: في التفسير
SAMIN-DURR:64:9/r8.claim: The loss is explained by wrongful wealth passing to an heir who obeys God with it, so the first owner enters Hell and the heir Paradise.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p137/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p137/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p137/r1.claim: The Gathering is Resurrection, when the first and last generations assemble on one plain, hear the caller, and are all visible, as other verses say.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p137/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p137/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p137/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas calls the Day of Mutual Loss one of Resurrection’s names and explains that Paradise’s people gain against Hell’s people; Qatada and Mujahid agree.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p137/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p137/r3.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p137/r3.claim: There is no greater loss than some people entering Paradise while others are consigned to Hell.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p12#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p12#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p12#2/r1.claim: The Day of Gathering brings every created community together for reckoning and recompense, from which some emerge as winners and others as losers.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p12#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p12#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p12#2/r2.claim: The Day of Mutual Loss is the only real loss because it is permanent and exposes each person’s hidden deficit before the whole assembly.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p12#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p12#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p12#2/r3.claim: The root gh-b-n concerns concealed loss, as in hidden bodily folds and a seller’s unnoticed loss in a transaction.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p12#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p12#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p12#2/r4.claim: Those entering Paradise are shown the place they would have occupied in Hell to increase gratitude, while those entering Hell see their lost place in Paradise and regret.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p12#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p12#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p12#2/r5.claim: Every unbeliever is cheated by rejecting faith, and believers lose through falling short in good works; worldly injustice cannot truly deprive the faithful.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p12#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p12#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p12#2/r6.claim: Remembering this day gives the strongest motive to obey commands and avoid prohibitions, lest one lose eternal reward.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p13/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p13/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p13/r1.claim: Faith must be renewed and confirmed by good deeds; God then conceals sins and admits believers to gardens with flowing rivers forever.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p13/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p13/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p13/r2.claim: The plural wording “khālidīn” emphasizes that all included believers share everlasting life, and “abadan” removes any doubt about its duration.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p13/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p13/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p13/r3.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read the verbs with first-person plural nūn, stressing that only God has power to forgive and admit people.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p13/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p13/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p13/r4.claim: “That is the great triumph” encompasses every benefit and removes every harm.

BURSEVI:v10p31#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p31#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p31#2/r2.claim: Righteous work must be free of ostentation, affectation, and deceit; the verse encourages others by explaining the honor and outcome of faith and good deeds.

BURSEVI:v10p31#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p31#2/r3.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v10p31#2/r3.claim: Faith alone does not guarantee good character, since believers are still commanded to act and refrain; good character can exist without faith, and both bring effects in either abode.

BURSEVI:v10p31#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p31#2/r4.speaker: العباس
BURSEVI:v10p31#2/r4.claim: Al-ʿAbbās asked whether Abū Ṭālib benefited from protecting the Prophet; the Prophet replied that it did, and without him Abū Ṭālib would be in Hell’s lowest depth.

BURSEVI:v10p31#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p31#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p31#2/r5.claim: A dream report says Abū Lahab was seen drinking water from his thumb on Mondays because he freed a servant who brought news of the Prophet’s birth.

BURSEVI:v10p31#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p31#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p31#2/r6.claim: Another report says a generous man was protected from Hell’s fire in an enclosure because of his generosity.

BURSEVI:v10p31#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p31#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p31#2/r7.claim: Faith is assent in the heart according to the stronger position, or assent plus confession for some; naming righteous action separately emphasizes it and encourages practice.

BURSEVI:v10p31#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p31#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p31#2/r8.claim: The four rivers beneath the gardens are those detailed in Sūrat Muḥammad.

BURSEVI:v10p7/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p7/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p7/r3.claim: ‘The day He gathers you’ either modifies ‘you will be informed’ or is recalled independently; the addressees are those first addressed by ‘Has there not come to you?’

BURSEVI:v10p7/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p7/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p7/r4.claim: The Gathering is Resurrection, when earlier and later people, jinn and humans, and heaven and earth assemble for reckoning and recompense; the definite article points to this known Day.

BURSEVI:v10p7/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p7/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p7/r5.claim: A report describes a caller heard by all creatures announcing the generous; a few who left their beds and praised God through hardship stand and are sent to Paradise before others are reckoned.

BURSEVI:v10p7/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p7/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p7/r6.claim: Other interpretations say God gathers each person with their deeds, the wrongdoer with the wronged, or every thing with its community.

BURSEVI:v10p7/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p7/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p7/r7.claim: Taghābun is mutual loss in a transaction through concealment; on Resurrection Day people lose as the blessed take places the doomed would have had, an ironic use because such placement is no real loss.

BURSEVI:v10p8#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p8#2/r1.speaker: إبراهيم بن أدهم
BURSEVI:v10p8#2/r1.claim: When a bathhouse attendant asked for the fee, Ibrāhīm ibn Adham wondered how anyone could enter the ‘house of the Lord’ without work if entry to the devil’s house costs a fee.

BURSEVI:v10p8#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p8#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p8#2/r2.claim: God erases believers’ sins on Resurrection Day and admits them to gardens by grace; rivers flow beneath their palaces or trees, and ‘forever’ confirms their stay has no end.

BURSEVI:v10p8#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p8#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p8#2/r3.claim: Singular pronouns first follow ‘whoever,’ then plural forms follow its collective meaning.

BURSEVI:v10p8#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p8#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p8#2/r4.claim: The great victory combines rescue from the greatest destruction with attainment of the finest pleasures; ‘large victory’ only brings benefits.

BURSEVI:v10p8#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p8#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p8#2/r5.claim: Inwardly, true victory is shedding illusory existence for real existence through experiential faith and righteous action; witnessing light illumines the relative self and opens gardens of union filled with knowledge.

BURSEVI:v10p8/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p8/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p8/r1.claim: A report says everyone meets God regretful: a wrongdoer regrets failing to do good, and a doer regrets failing to do more.

BURSEVI:v10p8/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p8/r2.speaker: بعض العارفين
BURSEVI:v10p8/r2.claim: Some gnostics say advancement in the afterlife is possible only in a station acquired in this life; a sought station attained now is a favor, while an unacquired one cannot be reached there, so progression ends at the Day of Loss.

BURSEVI:v10p8/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p8/r3.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v10p8/r3.claim: Some define loss as failing to recognize purity amid impurity and gentleness within apparent severity, becoming alienated from the Real through differentiation while truly in unity.

BURSEVI:v10p8/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p8/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p8/r4.claim: Those absorbed in reward and compensation experience loss; one absorbed in witnessing God has escaped it. Everyone loses when divine self-disclosure exceeds worldly unveilings and they realize they never fully knew or worshipped Him.

BURSEVI:v10p8/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p8/r5.speaker: ابن عطاء
BURSEVI:v10p8/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ says the people of truth differ in loss according to degrees of light at vision and manifestation.

BURSEVI:v10p8/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p8/r6.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v10p8/r6.claim: Some masters call the day of witnessing God in unity the loss of witnesses compared with veiled people, since the former enjoy nearness and union while the latter suffer distance and separation.

BURSEVI:v10p8/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p8/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p8/r7.claim: Faith must be sincere according to innate capacity; righteous work follows faith and seeks God’s face, whether obligatory or voluntary.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#2/r1.claim: “The day He gathers you” functions adverbially with the statement that you will be informed of your deeds.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#2/r2.claim: The statement that resurrection is easy for God confirms His power to raise the dead; the following call to believe renews the passage's appeal to believe in God, the Book, and its messenger.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#2/r3.claim: The call to believe is really the consequence of the earlier promise that people will be raised and informed, though it is advanced for emphasis and functions parenthetically.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#2/r4.claim: The closing statement that God knows what people do is a parenthesis within the preceding parenthesis and continues the exhortation, like saying, “act, for I am not unaware of you.”

ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#2/r5.speaker: الحوفي
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#2/r5.claim: Al-Ḥawfī treats the phrase as an adverb modifying khabīr; other authorities take khabīr to imply recompense, including both promise and threat.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes the opening time expression as meaning that God will punish them; al-Alusi questions this reading.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r10.speaker: غير واحد
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r10.claim: Others say people mutually lose by exchanging the positions they would have occupied had their outcomes been reversed.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r11.claim: A sound report says each entrant to Paradise is shown a place in the Fire he would have had by wrongdoing, and each entrant to the Fire a place in Paradise he missed.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r12.speaker: محيي السنة
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r12.claim: He defines loss as missing one's share: the unbeliever's lost Paradise and the believer's loss through falling short in good works become visible that day.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r13.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r13.claim: Al-Raghib distinguishes loss in a transaction of property from loss in judgment, and connects the Day's loss to the human bargain described in other verses.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r14.claim: The generic definite noun presents this as the real mutual loss, greater than even the greatest worldly losses, and the sentence is nominal.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r15.claim: The relative clause means whoever believes in God and does righteous work; God erases that person's sins on that Day and admits them to gardens forever.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r16.claim: The plural خالدين follows the meaning of من, while singular verbs follow its grammatical singular form.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r17.speaker: الأعرج وشيبة وأبو جعفر وطلحة ونافع وابن عامر والمفضل عن عاصم وزيد بن علي والحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r17.claim: These readers have نكفر and ندخله with the majestic first-person plural nūn in both verbs.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r18.claim: The great triumph is the forgiveness and admission to the Gardens: it combines rescue from immense ruin with attainment of the highest desires.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r2.claim: The punishment reading is ill suited because the passage urges action, while the warning was already completed in 64:7.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r3.claim: Another parsing makes the phrase an object governed by an implied اذكر, but it requires an ellipsis without a clear contextual clue.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r4.claim: Treating the phrase as a circumstantial time clause requires an unnecessary ellipsis, so the author prefers the first parsing he had discussed.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r5.claim: One reading has a silent ʿayn in يجمعكم, with a reported hint of the vowel; this is possible for the raised imperfect before an attached object pronoun.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r6.speaker: سلام ويعقوب وزيد بن علي والشعبي
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r6.claim: These readers recite نجمعكم with the first-person plural nūn.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r7.claim: The Gathering Day brings together the earlier and later peoples; this is clearer than the other proposed groups gathered there.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r8.claim: The lām may express purpose, with an implied phrase meaning for the reckoning on the Gathering Day, or it may mean في without ellipsis.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r9.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v28p123#3/r9.claim: They explain the Day of mutual loss as the day when Paradise's people gain at the expense of the people of the Fire; the one-sided verb form intensifies the loss.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p124/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p124/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p124/r1.claim: The promised triumph has no triumph beyond it because it includes escape from the greatest ruin and attainment of the highest desires.

ELMALILI:64:1-10#3/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:64:1-10#3/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:64:1-10#3/r16.claim: God will gather people for the Day of Gathering, the Day of Mutual Loss, when who gained and who lost becomes clear.

ELMALILI:64:1-10#4/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:64:1-10#4/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:64:1-10#4/r1.claim: Taghābun derives from gabn: losing or deceiving in a transaction or judgment, by selling or buying below or above value; mutual deception becomes manifest.

ELMALILI:64:1-10#4/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:64:1-10#4/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:64:1-10#4/r10.claim: The author prefers a definition broad enough to include both reciprocal and one-sided deception: the day real profit and loss are realized.

ELMALILI:64:1-10#4/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:64:1-10#4/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:64:1-10#4/r11.claim: Calling it mutual loss ironically addresses worldly people consumed by love of wealth who aim to deceive others; only the greatest final gain and loss are truly decisive.

ELMALILI:64:1-10#4/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:64:1-10#4/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:64:1-10#4/r12.claim: Whoever believes in God and does good for that day has sins covered and enters eternal gardens; the greatest triumph is safety and supreme divine pleasure.

ELMALILI:64:1-10#4/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:64:1-10#4/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:64:1-10#4/r2.claim: The source distinguishes gabn in commerce, pronounced with a silent bāʾ, from gaban in judgment, with both consonants vocalized.

ELMALILI:64:1-10#4/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:64:1-10#4/r3.speaker: Râgıb
ELMALILI:64:1-10#4/r3.claim: Raghib defines gabn as a concealed imbalance in dealings and says the Day of Mutual Loss reveals whether spiritual transactions gained or lost.

ELMALILI:64:1-10#4/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:64:1-10#4/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:64:1-10#4/r4.claim: The Qur'anic exchanges of selves and wealth for God's pleasure, or of God's covenant for a small price, will have their true profit or loss exposed that day.

ELMALILI:64:1-10#4/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:64:1-10#4/r5.speaker: some commentators
ELMALILI:64:1-10#4/r5.claim: Some say worldly objects will appear to people on that day in a measure contrary to what they had seemed to possess in life.

ELMALILI:64:1-10#4/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:64:1-10#4/r6.speaker: Bazı müfessirîn
ELMALILI:64:1-10#4/r6.claim: Some exegetes trace gabn to concealment, naming concealed bodily folds magābin and describing a woman as tayyibat al-magābin.

ELMALILI:64:1-10#4/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:64:1-10#4/r7.speaker: Keşşâf
ELMALILI:64:1-10#4/r7.claim: The Kashshaf reads mutual loss as a metaphor from trade: the saved occupy the places the wretched would have occupied, and vice versa.

ELMALILI:64:1-10#4/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:64:1-10#4/r8.speaker: Resûlullah
ELMALILI:64:1-10#4/r8.claim: A Prophetic report says each person entering Paradise is shown the place in Hell they would have occupied had they done evil, and each person entering Hell is shown the Paradise place they forfeited.

ELMALILI:64:1-10#4/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:64:1-10#4/r9.speaker: Mücâhid ve Katâde
ELMALILI:64:1-10#4/r9.claim: Mujahid and Qatada explain the day as the day when the people of Paradise deceive the people of Hell.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p274/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p274/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p274/r1.claim: The unexpressed subject of يجمعكم is God, named in the preceding verse.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p274/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p274/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p274/r2.claim: يجمعكم means gathering all people and nations; the Qur'an elsewhere calls it the gathering of you and the first generations.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p274/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p274/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p274/r3.claim: Alternatively, the gathering may mean resurrecting the bones, further confirming the resurrection the unbelievers denied.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p274/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p274/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p274/r4.claim: The lām in ليوم الجمع may express purpose: God gathers people for the appointed day on which everyone is gathered for judgment; the two uses of gathering form wordplay, not circular reasoning.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p274/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p274/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p274/r5.claim: Another grammatical possibility makes the lām mean في, as in expressions for an event occurring at or in its time.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p274/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p274/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p274/r6.claim: He prefers the lām of timing, meaning عند: people are gathered at the appointed time without delay, rebutting their denial of resurrection.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p274/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p274/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p274/r7.claim: يوم الجمع is the Day of Resurrection and a title for it; a hadith says God gathers the first and last generations.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p274/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p274/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p274/r8.claim: The sentence interrupts the link between the prior warning that deeds will be disclosed and the promise to believers, magnifying the Day and warning idolaters of loss.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p275/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p275/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p275/r1.claim: The demonstrative instead of a pronoun draws attention to this Day and, as a distant demonstrative, suggests its elevated rank.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p275/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p275/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p275/r2.claim: Taghabun is the reciprocal verbal noun of غابن; the reciprocal form ordinarily describes an act shared by two or more parties.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p275/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p275/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p275/r3.claim: A sale's غبن is selling below fair value, making the seller the loser; the word extends metaphorically to loss generally, as al-Aʿsha's verse shows.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p275/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p275/r4.speaker: الأعشى
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p275/r4.claim: The cited line uses غبن الخاسر to attest the word's sense of loss.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p275/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p275/r5.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة والحسن
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p275/r5.claim: The majority of exegetes take the reciprocal literally: the people of Paradise have gained over the people of Hell, each receiving the other's contrasting outcome.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p275/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p275/r6.speaker: القرطبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p275/r6.claim: Al-Qurtubi and others explain the reported view as an analogy between the two groups and traders, one receiving fair value and the other a defrauded price.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p275/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p275/r7.speaker: الراغب وابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p275/r7.claim: A minority understand the reciprocal form as intensity or abundance, a metaphor for the great loss of the disbelievers rather than mutual exchange.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p276/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p276/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p276/r1.claim: He takes the reciprocal form figuratively for abundant loss; the disbelievers suffer this loss, with God as the one who causes it.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p276/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p276/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p276/r2.claim: The verse threatens idolaters with their severe loss on the Day of Gathering, in the context of the call to believe in God, His Messenger, and the revealed Light.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p276/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p276/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p276/r3.claim: Restricting the Day of Loss makes sense because believers gain greatly on that Day; he compares the contrast with failed trade and the Prophet's definition of the bankrupt person.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p276/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p276/r4.speaker: النبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p276/r4.claim: The cited hadith identifies the true bankrupt person as one who is bankrupt on the Day of Resurrection.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p276/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p276/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p276/r5.claim: Defining both parts of the sentence restricts the kind of Day of Loss to this Day alone; worldly market losses count as negligible by comparison.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p276/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p276/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p276/r6.claim: The definite article in التغابن marks the genus of loss; other verses contrast ultimate loss with commerce that never fails.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p276/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p276/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p276/r7.claim: He calls this the decisive interpretation and criticizes commentators for passing over the verse's rhetorical force.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p276/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p276/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p276/r8.claim: The promise to believers coordinates with the command to believe in 64:8 and spells out what God's comprehensive knowledge means.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p276/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p276/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p276/r9.claim: The conditional promise includes any polytheist who believes after this admonition; السيئات means disbelief and earlier corrupt deeds.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p277/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p277/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p277/r1.claim: Expiating sins means pardoning liability for them; the intensive form derives metaphorically from covering something in order to remove it, as with forgiveness.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p277/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p277/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p277/r2.claim: صالحا describes an omitted verbal noun, with the implied wording عملا صالحا.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p277/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p277/r3.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وأبو جعفر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p277/r3.claim: These readers use first-person plural نكفر and ندخله, shifting from third person to a welcoming first-person promise.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p277/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p277/r4.speaker: باقي القراء
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p277/r4.claim: The other readers keep the third-person forms, following the apparent discourse and the preceding mention of God.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p277/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p277/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p277/r5.claim: ذلك الفوز العظيم is a concluding summary of the promise.

TABATABAI:64:9-10/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:64:9-10/r1.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:64:9-10/r1.claim: Some commentators explain taghabun by the following promise and warning through the phrase about the evil destination; the author says that reading is not very apparent.

TABATABAI:64:9-10/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:64:9-10/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:64:9-10/r3.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that a Paradise entrant is shown the Fire seat they would have occupied by wrongdoing, increasing gratitude, while a Fire entrant sees the Paradise seat they would have had by righteousness, increasing regret.

TABATABAI:64:9-10/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:64:9-10/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:64:9-10/r4.claim: Many narrations with this meaning exist in Sunni and Shiite sources, and some were cited earlier under the beginning of 23:1.

TABATABAI:64:9-10/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:64:9-10/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:64:9-10/r5.claim: A report defines the Day of Mutual Loss as the day Paradise's people wrongfully gain over Hell's people; it also identifies the meeting, calling, and regret days and says death is slaughtered.

TABATABAI:64:9-10/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:64:9-10/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:64:9-10/r6.claim: Reports interpreting the surah's opening verses through allegiance—faith and unbelief as allegiance, clear proofs as Imams, and light as the Imam—address its inner sense and are not literal exegesis.

TABATABAI:64:9/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:64:9/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:64:9/r1.claim: The Day of Assembly is the Resurrection, when people are gathered for judgment; the phrase functions as a time adverb for the prior promise of resurrection and disclosure.

TABATABAI:64:9/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:64:9/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:64:9/r2.claim: Other verses explain this gathering as God's adjudication and separation of disputes, including 18:99, 45:17, 2:113, and 32:25.

TABATABAI:64:9/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:64:9/r3.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:64:9/r3.claim: Al-Raghib defines ghubn as secretly undervaluing another party in a transaction and reads the Day of Mutual Loss through profitable or losing exchanges people made in life.

TABATABAI:64:9/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:64:9/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:64:9/r4.claim: The first account is attractive but does not fit the apparent reciprocal form of taghabun, which suggests parties acting upon one another.

TABATABAI:64:9/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:64:9/r5.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:64:9/r5.claim: A second view says people will discover that things differ from their worldly estimates; the author finds it subtle and sees support in descriptions of unexpected afterlife rewards and disclosures.

TABATABAI:64:9/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:64:9/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:64:9/r6.claim: On this second account, all gathered people experience mutual loss: believers regret not doing more for the next life, unbelievers did nothing, and both failed to value that Day; the author notes the preceding objection applies too.

TABATABAI:64:9/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:64:9/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:64:9/r7.claim: A third account sees leaders and followers in error each causing the other's loss: leaders mislead followers toward worldly life, while followers enable leaders' arrogance.

TABATABAI:64:9/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:64:9/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:64:9/r8.claim: A narrated fourth account says each person would have had a Paradise dwelling by obedience and a Fire dwelling by sin; the transfer of dwellings makes believers the winners and unbelievers the losers.

ASAD-NOTES:64:8#n8/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:64:8#n8/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:64:8#n8/r1.claim: An added 'time' is needed to make sense of the accusative yawma in the following phrase.

ASAD-NOTES:64:intro/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:64:intro/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:64:intro/r3.claim: The word taghabun in verse 9 became the surah's identifying keyword.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p341/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p341/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p341/r1.claim: Al-Taghābun continues al-Munāfiqūn’s warning about wealth, children, charity, and death: worldly life is not final, and the Hereafter reveals success or failure.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p341/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p341/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p341/r2.claim: To attain the Hereafter’s great success, one must be ready to sacrifice for God and His Messenger despite reproach; family love may weaken resolve, so regard family as a trial while forgiving them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p341/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p341/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p341/r5.claim: People are urged to believe in God, His Prophet, and the Qur’an and prepare for the Day that decides victor and vanquished.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p342/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p342/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p342/r1.claim: The gathering day distinguishes winners from losers: believers who do good receive eternal Paradise, while disbelievers who reject revelation remain in Hell.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p349/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p349/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p349/r1.claim: The gathering is certain under God's scheme, supported by signs within and around humanity and by the testimony of prophets, messengers, and scriptures.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p349/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p349/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p349/r2.claim: The references to assembling all people on one appointed day refute doubts that anyone could gather the countless inhabitants of land and sea.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p349/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p349/r3.speaker: Shāh ‘Abd al-Qādir
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p349/r3.claim: Shāh ʿAbd al-Qādir translates yawm al-tagābun as the day of victory and defeat; Islahi calls this translation very accurate.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p349/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p349/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p349/r4.claim: The verse explains victory and defeat through the final outcomes: believers are forgiven and enter eternal gardens, while deniers enter Hell forever.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p349/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p349/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p349/r5.claim: People wrongly treat worldly luxury or deprivation as victory or defeat; this world is a trial, and true victors are faithful doers of good in the Hereafter.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p350/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p350/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p350/r1.claim: Hereafter's victory belongs to faithful people who did good even if they had little worldly provision; those who lacked faith lose even if affluent.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p350/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p350/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p350/r2.claim: Those who see worldly life as success fear future need and hesitate to sacrifice; those oriented to the Hereafter spend for its lasting success.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r11.claim: The term taghabun comes from a root with meanings including concealing, forgetting, erring, weakness, and deceiving; in law, gabn is a marked imbalance between exchanged values.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r12.claim: As a reciprocal tafa'ul form, taghabun commonly means deceiving one another or both deceiving and being deceived.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r13.speaker: İbn Atıyye
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r13.claim: He says the form need not be reciprocal; as in tawadu, it can indicate the intensity or abundance of an action.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r14.speaker: Birçok müfessir
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r14.claim: Many exegetes see an allusion to disbelievers and hypocrites trading faith for unbelief and the Hereafter for worldly life.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r15.speaker: Bazılarına göre
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r15.claim: Some understand the term to mean that things will appear different in quantity and value on Judgment Day.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r16.speaker: Bazılarına göre
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r16.claim: Another reading says Judgment Day reveals the real profit in spiritual transactions: selling God's covenant cheaply or God purchasing believers' lives and property for Paradise.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r17.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r17.claim: Considering these interpretations and the context, the author renders the phrase as the day when loss and gain become clear.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r5.claim: At the Gathering, real profit and loss become clear, and believers who live well through virtuous deeds receive reward.

QIRAAT-ER:64:9:17#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:64:9:17#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:64:9:17#1/r1.claim: First-person plural makes God's expiation explicit in direct divine speech.

QIRAAT-ER:64:9:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:64:9:2#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:64:9:2#1/r1.claim: First-person plural turns the divine agency from third-person reference into direct divine speech.

QIRAAT-ER:64:9:21#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:64:9:21#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:64:9:21#1/r1.claim: The first-person plural admits him, matching the We form in the preceding expiation variant.

STUDYQURAN:64:9/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:64:9/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:64:9/r1.claim: The Day of Gathering is Resurrection, when all people across generations and all jinn assemble on a barren plain for judgment, each community behind its prophet, and all living things ultimately gather to their Lord.

STUDYQURAN:64:9/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:64:9/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:64:9/r2.claim: The phrase may also refer to God gathering people’s bones to resurrect them, answering disbelievers who object that bones and dust cannot become a new creation.

STUDYQURAN:64:9/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:64:9/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:64:9/r3.claim: Taghābun derives from ghabana, “to stint or shortchange another in a transaction,” with an implication of deception or subterfuge.

STUDYQURAN:64:9/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:64:9/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:64:9/r4.claim: The term most likely refers to Resurrection because humans cannot fully repay God for what He has done, even though every soul is paid fully for its own deeds.

STUDYQURAN:64:9/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:64:9/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:64:9/r5.claim: Believers are described as selling their souls for God’s pleasure and exchanging worldly life for the Hereafter; God purchases their souls and wealth for the Garden in a one-sided transaction.

STUDYQURAN:64:9/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:64:9/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:64:9/r6.claim: Those who sell God’s covenant and oaths for a small price shortchange themselves; they have traded guidance for error and will not be rightly guided.

STUDYQURAN:64:9/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:64:9/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:64:9/r7.claim: By contrast, those who sell their souls for God have their sins absolved in this life and enter Paradise in the next; attaining the Garden is called the great triumph.

STUDYQURAN:64:9/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:64:9/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:64:9/r8.claim: The image of entering Gardens with rivers running below is discussed in relation to several other verses.

STUDYQURAN:64:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:64:intro/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:64:intro/r4.claim: The sūrah’s title comes from its unique description of the Judgment Day as the Day of Mutual Dispossession.
